name: DGX Spark GLM-5.3 Flash FP4-Local Atlas (SparkGLM 0.3.6)

sparks.description: How many DGX Sparks serve the model: 2 is a TP-2 pair over a direct cable, 4 is TP-4 over a daisy chain.

2.description: Two directly connected Sparks, tensor and expert parallelism 2, profile 4x1m.

4.description: Four Sparks cabled as a chain, tensor and expert parallelism 4, profile 4x1m-tp4.

drafter.description: The DFlash2 drafter for speculative decoding.

v81.description: Enntity's v81 (private repository; needs access to Enntity/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2-enntity).

v80.description: Enntity's v80 (private repository Enntity/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2-enntity, pinned under its earlier name Enntity/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2-enntity-v80, which redirects).

dflash2.description: incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2, the reference drafter (Apache-2.0 from the pinned revision).

memory.description: How much of each Spark's memory the model takes. Speed is the same; only the prompt cache pool changes.

full.description: The qualified setting: 114 GB a Spark, for Sparks that run nothing else.

shared.description: 108 GB a Spark (GPU memory utilization 0.88), for a Spark that also hosts about 10 GB of other services. The model takes 105 to 106 GB before any prompt cache, so the cache pool is small. Four streams only: the 8-stream profile does not fit.

streams.description: How many requests decode at once on a two-Spark pair. Four Sparks always run 4.

4.description: Four streams with a 1M-token context each (profile 4x1m).

8.description: Eight streams with a 128K-token context each (profile 8x128k): more total throughput for many short requests, such as parallel section writing.

model.description: The checkpoint the engine serves. Either is served under the same gateway id, glm-5.3-flash-atlas, so routes and aliases stay as they are.

glm-5.3-flash.description: nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-FP4-Local as published (NVIDIA Open Model Agreement; base model MIT).

sage-s2.1-flash.description: Enntity/Sage-S2.1-Flash-NVFP4 (MIT), a calibrated NVFP4 quantization of internlm/Sage-S2.1-Flash in the same layout, 179 GB. Text, images and video; Sage's scientific-input projectors are not included. Qualified on two Sparks with dflash2.

summary: SparkGLM on two directly connected DGX Sparks (TP-2 pair) or four cabled as a daisy chain (TP-4), serving nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-FP4-Local as published with DFlash2 speculative decoding: four requests of up to 1M tokens. Options: --sparks 2|4, --drafter v81|v80|dflash2 and --model glm53-flash|sage-s21-flash. Additive only: no default model, no aliases.
description: This recipe installs SparkGLM 0.3.6, as republished on 2026-11-25, at the immutable product revision recorded in backends/atlas-sparkglm/pins-0.3.6-7880aee26de2.json, on two Sparks (--sparks 2, a TP-2 pair over the private fabric) or four (--sparks 4, TP-4 over a switchless daisy chain, rank 0-1-2-3 along the cables), with any of three drafters (--drafter v81 or v80, Enntity's from a private repository, or --drafter dflash2, incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2). Without --drafter, both sizes use dflash2. --model sage-s2.1-flash serves Enntity/Sage-S2.1-Flash-NVFP4 in place of the GLM checkpoint, under the same gateway id. Setup remembers the options it installed with. LLooM owns orchestration, admission, worker-first startup, readiness, routing and telemetry. The Atlas engine image is built from Enntity/sparkglm by that repository's install/build.sh; LLooM commits no engine source. The engine (Atlas-Inf/atlas, on the Enntity/atlas spark branch) is AGPL-3.0-only and runs from its own container image. Setup acquires the pinned checkpoint and the selected drafter and pulls the pinned image from GHCR by its immutable manifest digest (image.reference; the mutable tag is never pulled); the serving path only ever starts the prepared image. The checkpoint is served as published, with no overlay. One image serves both sizes. 0.3.6 is 0.3.5's engine plus one fix (Enntity/atlas#33). With tool_choice required or naming a tool, the first token of the call is the native <tool_call> token; the tag spelled out as text is no longer legal there. GLM-5.3-Flash FP4-Local already opened a forced call with the native token, so its output is unchanged. A checkpoint of the same architecture that ranks the text form first (Sage S2.1 Flash) returned forced calls as plain text on 0.3.5 and passes 109/109 on 0.3.6 where it passed 97/109. On a pair in Spark mode with dflash2 it qualified on 2026-11-18 against 0.3.5: identical greedy output and prompt logprobs, 109/109 live checks, and one RigMark round level with 0.3.5 (prose 37.7 against 37.6 tok/s, code 66.1 against 65.9, structured 88.8 against 87.7). That run used GPU memory utilization 0.90 under a 113 GB budget where this recipe sets 0.91 and 114 GB, because its head had about 0.3 GB less memory available than the 114 GB budget needs. On 2026-11-18 it was installed through this recipe on all four Sparks, each pulling the image by digest. On a pair, at this recipe's 0.91 and 114 GB, its greedy output and prompt logprobs were identical to the qualification run's, and its Strict output and its image and video output were identical to 0.3.5's. On a four-Spark chain its greedy output and prompt logprobs were identical to 0.3.5's, with the same 107/109 live checks and speed level (prose 57.5 against 58.3 tok/s, code 106.5 against 106.9, structured 146.8 against 146.2). The four-Spark run used GPU memory utilization 0.69 under a 90 GB budget where this recipe sets 0.88 and 114 GB, because two Sparks of that chain host other services; Strict mode and images were not run on four Sparks. Version 8 pins the image republished on 2026-11-25: the product's launchers now default to Spark mode, which this recipe already sets, and its engine adds Enntity/atlas#38, a build-time test fix with no serving change. It installs the same checkpoints, drafters and options as version 7.

provenance.source: SparkGLM 0.3.6: Enntity/sparkglm e2ee39ae3fd7a2235085ddd0fb1aa52177e9875b (main, 0.3.6 as republished 2026-11-25, install tree 7880aee26de26549c573095597285c3a8b88df17), engine Enntity/atlas spark @ 6bb95b52c173f2df488a74a7d3570c50110b8f6c (0.3.5's 59ead299 plus Enntity/atlas#33 and #38; AGPL-3.0-only, recorded in the image's /opt/atlas/source-manifest.json). The install pulls ghcr.io/enntity/atlas-sparkglm@sha256:52672349a0527ce28e49b1564c20f8045296ef46d1dae903d67c9cbd8f76b537 by digest (pins-0.3.6-7880aee26de2.json; the tags ghcr.io/enntity/atlas-sparkglm:7880aee26de2 and :0.3.6 are never pulled), and each host verifies the image's io.enntity.sparkglm.install-tree label, arm64 architecture, both profiles and the engine commit. Model nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-FP4-Local revision 76348ddb2be2e35e39ecfc00e75dc07703f4f3d5 (NVIDIA Open Model Agreement; base model MIT) is served as published. With --model sage-s2.1-flash the checkpoint is Enntity/Sage-S2.1-Flash-NVFP4 revision 6967e49571a951ac0c71bb554eeeca365e838130 (MIT) instead. Drafters: Enntity/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2-enntity revision ee5ed56e3ed2e59fd2d5177fe6773b2f6fb4aa80 (v81, tag v81, model.safetensors sha256 d14e1edb080711d4; private), Enntity/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2-enntity-v80 revision 8416cdfbf4cfb302b86a058cb5f5b89f891350c0 (v80, the same repository under its earlier name; private) and incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2 revision 6cc6c481eee930a5139619ed919f78726371adbc (Apache-2.0). Qualified at TP-2 on 2026-11-18 against 0.3.5, then installed through this recipe, and in Strict mode and with images against 0.3.5 and on a four-Spark chain against 0.3.5.

hardware.testedMachine: Two directly connected DGX Spark systems (--sparks 2) or four cabled as a daisy chain (--sparks 4)
notes: SparkGLM 0.3.6. 0.3.6 is 0.3.5's engine plus one fix (Enntity/atlas#33). With tool_choice required or naming a tool, the first token of the call is the native <tool_call> token; the tag spelled out as text is no longer legal there. GLM-5.3-Flash FP4-Local already opened a forced call with the native token, so its output is unchanged. A checkpoint of the same architecture that ranks the text form first (Sage S2.1 Flash) returned forced calls as plain text on 0.3.5 and passes 109/109 on 0.3.6 where it passed 97/109. On a pair in Spark mode with dflash2 it qualified on 2026-11-18 against 0.3.5: identical greedy output and prompt logprobs, 109/109 live checks, and one RigMark round level with 0.3.5 (prose 37.7 against 37.6 tok/s, code 66.1 against 65.9, structured 88.8 against 87.7). That run used GPU memory utilization 0.90 under a 113 GB budget where this recipe sets 0.91 and 114 GB, because its head had about 0.3 GB less memory available than the 114 GB budget needs. On 2026-11-18 it was installed through this recipe on all four Sparks, each pulling the image by digest. On a pair, at this recipe's 0.91 and 114 GB, its greedy output and prompt logprobs were identical to the qualification run's, and its Strict output and its image and video output were identical to 0.3.5's. On a four-Spark chain its greedy output and prompt logprobs were identical to 0.3.5's, with the same 107/109 live checks and speed level (prose 57.5 against 58.3 tok/s, code 106.5 against 106.9, structured 146.8 against 146.2). The four-Spark run used GPU memory utilization 0.69 under a 90 GB budget where this recipe sets 0.88 and 114 GB, because two Sparks of that chain host other services; Strict mode and images were not run on four Sparks.

With --model sage-s2.1-flash the same image serves Enntity/Sage-S2.1-Flash-NVFP4 at revision 6967e495 in place of the GLM checkpoint, under the same gateway id: a calibrated NVFP4 quantization of internlm/Sage-S2.1-Flash (MIT), 179 GB, laid out as this engine loads it. Installed with this option on a pair on 2026-11-18, in Spark mode with dflash2, it passed 109/109 live checks and decoded 38.6 / 67.9 / 90.0 tok/s (prose, code, structured) against GLM-5.3-Flash's 37.7 / 66.1 / 88.8 on the same pair and image. Sage leaves a slightly smaller prompt cache: in consecutive starts on the same pair the pool read 2.22M tokens with Sage and 2.38M with GLM-5.3-Flash, and it varies by a few percent from start to start. Sage with four Sparks, --memory shared or --streams 8 was not run, and the drafters were trained on GLM-5.3-Flash, not on Sage.

With --sparks 2 the pair uses tensor and expert parallelism 2 across the private ConnectX RoCE fabric; each node needs cluster.nodes[ID].fabricHca and fabricInterface. With --sparks 4 the ranks follow cluster.nodes[ID].fabricChain on a switchless chain, rank 0 leads, and the workers start from the far end.

Every Spark reserves 114 GiB with a 4096 MiB OOM guard. TP-2 raises GPU memory utilization to 0.91 with the display carveout and shards KV across the pair; TP-4 uses the profile's 0.88 with neither, and leaves no room for sidecars.
The disk prefix cache is 48 GB at TP-2 and off at TP-4, where it is not qualified.

Licenses: the Atlas engine in the image is AGPL-3.0-only (not included in LLooM). The v81 and v80 drafters are Enntity's, from a private repository; incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2 is Apache-2.0 from the pinned revision 6cc6c481; nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-FP4-Local is under the NVIDIA Open Model Agreement (base model MIT); Enntity/Sage-S2.1-Flash-NVFP4 is MIT, as internlm/Sage-S2.1-Flash is.
All Sparks must carry the same pins, the same backend directory, the same checkpoint and drafter, and LLooM configs that name the same cluster leader.
